paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. God's commands aren't suggestions, and He takes them seriously. A man gathers wood on the Sabbath, and the LORD says, "The man must surely be put to death." (Numbers 15:35) That one is heavy, and I'm not going to joke about it.

But look at what God does right after. He doesn't leave His people to white-knuckle it alone. He tells them to make tassels with a blue cord, "for you to look at, so that you may remember all the commandments of the LORD." (Numbers 15:39) God gave them something to see, because He knows how easily we forget. I once forgot where I put my own timer while it was HANGING around my neck!

And here's the part for you, baker. Our own heart and our own eyes can lead us off the path, and God says so plainly in Numbers 15:39. His answer is to give us reminders and then call us to obey and be holy to Him. (Numbers 15:40) He ends with "I am the LORD your God who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God." (Numbers 15:41) So find your own blue cord, friend, whether that's a verse on the fridge or a morning in the Word, and look at it often.
